title: Your baptism day
hookLine: celebrate the day you became a child of God
tomorrow: so who's your saint if your name isn't on the calendar?

lines: A CARD IN THE WRONG MONTH.
HOW CAN A MAN BE BORN WHEN HE IS OLD?
cards: A card on a grandmother's fridge, in the wrong month. It's for her grandson's baptism day, and she calls it his first birthday. Odd, since he was born weeks before.
A grown man brought Jesus the same puzzle, at night. Nicodemus, a teacher, hears that a man must be born again, and asks, in the Douay-Rheims: "How can a man be born when he is old?" Fair question.
You only get born once. Don't you?

teach.b: Jesus answers with water: "unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God." That's the first birthday in the grandmother's sense.
Catholics hold that baptism is a real birth: the Catechism says the baptized are reborn as children of God, and calls baptism the door to the other sacraments. A birth, so it has a date.

teach.h: BURIED WITH HIM, RAISED TO WALK.
teach.b: Then Paul adds a twist, in Romans: "For we are buried together with him by baptism into death," so that, like Christ rising, we may walk in newness of life. A burial and a birth in one bath.
That's the puzzle solved: the day isn't about getting wet, it's about a life starting.

teach.h: A DATE IN THE PARISH BOOK.
teach.b: One to tell a friend: Church law asks the parish to write each baptism in its register, so the date of yours, if you were baptized, is likely sitting in a book in that church.
Pope Francis once asked a crowd at a general audience to find out that date and celebrate it like a birthday.
Some families light the white candle from that day, the one the parents were handed with the words, receive the light of Christ.

how: The parish where someone was baptized records the date in its baptismal register; some Catholic families mark the anniversary by lighting the baptismal candle or renewing baptismal promises.

o: the day your life as a child of God began
the day a teen chooses to join the parish
the day a baby is given a saint's name

games.q: your little cousin was baptized in March but her birthday is in January. she asks why grandma bakes her two cakes. what do you tell her?
o: one for the day you were born, one for the day your life with God began.
the second cake is for the saint whose name you were given.
grandma likes cake; baptism is just a nice family party.
games.why: Catholics call baptism a new birth, so it gets its own day: born of water and the Spirit, a first birthday in God's family.

practice: Pick up your phone and text one person who'd know: a parent, a godparent, the parish office. Ask for your baptism date, or, if you weren't baptized, the date of someone you love.
While you wait for the answer, sit with the words newness of life. If you pray, you can thank God for that day.

wordCard.voice: Your baptism day. The date a life in God's family began, kept by some families with a candle and a cake. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: baptism, the word the New Testament uses for the washing.

carryVoice: The line to keep: your first birthday, written in a parish book with your name. Until tomorrow.
